hive: 🐝 Good day, sir. Dabba Days is set up on your computer and nothing has been built yet, so we're starting with a clean slate. What shall we build first?
We haven't met properly yet. Say "set me up" and I'll get to know your business or your product in about two minutes, or help you start something new.
🐝 Let's get you set up. First, which of these is you?
Very good. 5 quick steps, about two minutes. Say skip to any, or stop to carry on later; I keep everything as you go.

1 of 5. Your business.
What is it called, what does it do, and who are your customers? A line or two is plenty (🎙 a voice note works too).
✅ Got it, Dabba Days: Home cooks make lunch and we deliver it to office workers. Our customers are people working in offices. We deliver in Bengaluru.

2 of 5. Where it runs.
Where can I see it? Send its web address.

3 of 5. Numbers and data.
I already have the code here (15 files). So I can answer things like "how many orders this week?", send me any of these, as many as you like:
• an admin or analytics address, with its key
• a database address (please a read-only login)
• a shared spreadsheet link, or a CSV or Excel file

I only ever read; I never change your data. Keys stay on this computer. Say done when finished.

✅ dabba database: I can see 8 tables: complaints, cooks, customers, deliveries, payments, payouts, plans, subscriptions.

Anything else? Or say done.

4 of 5. How you run things.
Anything written down: policies, FAQ, price list, a pitch deck? Send the files here (PDF, text, CSV), or tell me in a few lines. Say done when finished.
📚 Read: 13 things kept, and 6 rules for how the product behaves. Anything else, or done?

5 of 5. Hosting.
Vercel, Netlify, Render, Railway, Fly or Azure? Or say don't know.

✅ All set, Dabba Days. I know 18 things about your business; read-only access to dabba database.

From now on, just tell me what you want. For example:
• "how many orders this week?"
• "show me the pricing page on desktop"
• "I want more repeat buyers"
• "add a referral page"

I'll ask only what I can't work out myself: your own rules for the unusual cases.

🐝 Sir, on paper it is simple: a cook earns Rs 70 for every lunch they make, paid each Monday for the previous week. The product's own calculation does exactly that, and the 161 payouts since August all match it and all landed on the Monday. Your records also show something the policy never mentions: a Rs 500 "clean month" bonus, added to the last payout of the month. I checked it against the complaints, and it went to every cook with zero complaints that month and to none of the others, without exception, in August, September and October. Is that your rule, Sir? If so, it deserves a line in the policy and a place on the cook sign-up page.

plan.title: A shorter sign-up form
plan.why: Sign-up asks for 9 things, including a company GST number that most office workers don't have, and says every field is required before it charges the first month, so many people will stop there.
plan.seen: signup.html: name, email, phone, company, company GST number, office address, floor and desk number, area, plan; 'All fields are required. Your first month is charged today.'
plan.build: In signup.html, keep name, phone, email, office address, area and plan as required (add the `required` attribute to them). Make company name and floor/desk number optional and put '(optional)' in their labels. Handle the GST field according to the owner's answer: either mark it optional with the label 'Company GST number (optional, only if your company needs a GST invoice)', or remove it. Replace 'All fields are required.' with a line under the plan select that shows the chosen plan's price ('Veg Basic · ₹2,400 / month, 20 lunches'), and keep 'Your first month is charged today.' Change the button to 'Pay ₹… and subscribe' using a few lines of inline JS that update the price when the plan changes (2,400 / 3,000 / 3,400). Add a test to test_dabba.py that reads signup.html and checks that name="gst" is either absent or has no `required` attribute, that name="desk" has no `required` attribute, and that 'All fields are required' no longer appears.
plan.decide: Do you need a company GST number from people who subscribe?

plan.title: Show 'cancel anytime' and fix the cancel link
plan.why: No page says people can cancel whenever they like, so signing up looks like a lock-in, and an existing subscriber who clicks 'Cancel my subscription' gets nowhere.
plan.seen: subscription-options.html: 'Cancel my subscription' links to '#'; plans.html and signup.html never mention cancelling.
plan.build: Create cancel.html in the same layout as pause.html (same header, nav and footer). Use the heading 'Cancel my subscription' and the text 'You can cancel anytime. Your lunches carry on until the end of this month, and your plan won't renew next month. There is no refund for the current month.' Below that, add a form with a 'Cancel my subscription' button and a link to pause.html: 'Just away for a while? Pause for up to 10 days instead.' In subscription-options.html, change href="#" on the cancel link to cancel.html and keep the pause link. On plans.html, under 'Billed monthly.', add 'Cancel anytime. Your plan simply stops renewing at the end of the month.' Add the same line to the muted note on signup.html. Tests: add cancel.html to test_pages_exist, assert that subscription-options.html contains href="cancel.html" and no href="#", and assert that plans.html contains 'Cancel anytime'.

plan.title: Explain skips, holidays and refunds on the plans page
plan.why: Office workers take leave, have holidays and worry about paying for lunches they don't get, but the plans page only lists prices. The ₹100 skip credit, the 10-day pause, free public holidays and full refunds for missed lunches only appear on pages inside the account, or nowhere.
plan.seen: plans.html: only '20 lunches a month… Billed monthly.' and three prices. skip.html and pause.html (reached only from My account) explain skips and pauses. No page mentions Karnataka public holidays, refunds for missed lunches or same-day replies to complaints. billing.py has SKIP_CREDIT_RS=100 and M
plan.build: On plans.html, between the plan cards and the Subscribe button, add a card titled 'You only pay for lunches you get' with these 5 short lines: 'Skip a lunch before 9 pm the night before: ₹100 off your next bill.' / 'Going away? Pause for up to 10 days a month. Paused days aren't charged.' / 'No lunch and no charge on Karnataka public holidays.' / 'If your cook is ill we send another cook from your area. If no one can cook, that lunch is refunded in full.' / 'Lunch didn't arrive? It's always refunded, and we answer complaints the same day.' Use the existing .card style. Under the 'Skip any day' card on index.html, change the text to 'Skip before 9 pm the night before and get ₹100 off your next bill.' Add a test that reads plans.html and checks that it contains '₹100', '9 pm', '10 days' and 'public holiday', so the page stays in line with the rules in billing.py.
